# Astra ECS v3.1 - Hardening: Scheduler Seam, TypeContext, Container Fixes & CI

## Release Highlights

Astra 3.1 is a hardening release focused on correctness, portability, and safe integration patterns. It ships a clean threading seam (no surprise thread spawning), process-shared type identity for multi-module and DLL scenarios, two container correctness fixes found by new fuzz suites, and a GitHub Actions CI matrix covering MSVC, gcc, and clang (distro-default on ubuntu-latest; verified locally with gcc 15.1 / clang 18). The public API is backward-compatible; two deprecated footguns (`TypeID_v` and `MakeComponentMask` constexpr) are removed.

---

## Parallel Execution & The Scheduler Seam

The old `View::ParallelForEach`, `Relations::ParallelForEachDescendant`, and `ParallelExecutor` implementations spawned `std::async` tasks ad-hoc per call. Benchmarking at 1 M entities with a trivial store-only kernel showed this was actively harmful: the ad-hoc async path took **2.43 ms** against **1.53 ms** for the sequential path -- a 1.59x loss due to thread-pool contention and synchronisation overhead on a memory-bound kernel.

### IWorkScheduler seam

A thin scheduler interface lives at `Core/WorkScheduler.hpp`:

```cpp
class IWorkScheduler {
public:
    virtual ~IWorkScheduler() = default;
    virtual void ParallelFor(size_t count, size_t minBatch,
                             const std::function<void(size_t, size_t)>& fn) = 0;
    virtual size_t WorkerCount() const noexcept = 0;
};
```

Inject via `Registry::Config::workScheduler` (`std::shared_ptr<IWorkScheduler>`). When `nullptr` (the new default), all parallel APIs run sequentially inline -- safe in single-threaded contexts and faster on memory-bound workloads.

```cpp
// Sequential (default -- fastest for memory-bound kernels)
Astra::Registry registry;

// Parallel with your own pool
auto scheduler = std::make_shared<MyEnkiTSAdapter>();
Astra::Registry::Config config;
config.workScheduler = scheduler;
Astra::Registry registry(config);
```

The reference fork-join pool is available in `tests/Support/TestWorkerPool.hpp` for test and benchmark use. With the injected test pool on a **compute-heavy** kernel at 1 M entities: **2.17 ms** (injected pool) vs 2.43 ms (old ad-hoc async) -- an 11% improvement once thread overhead is no longer paid per-call. Sequential remains the right default; parallelism pays when the kernel is compute-bound rather than memory-bound. For the store-only (memory-bound) kernel, sequential at **1.53 ms** still wins; the default is now sequential rather than the silently-losing parallel path.

## Multi-Module & DLL Support

Static `typeindex`-based IDs break across DLL boundaries because each module gets its own static. `TypeContext` (`Core/TypeContext.hpp`) replaces the old scheme with process-shared type identity.

### How it works

- **Stable XXHash64 type-name hashes** are the cross-module identity key.
- **Dense sequential ComponentIDs** are assigned from the shared context and are mask-compatible with the existing archetype bitmask system.
- A pending static-registration queue is drained when `SetTypeContext` is called from each module, so components registered before the context is installed are not lost.
- `MetaRegistry` now lives inside the context; the singleton API (`MetaRegistry::Instance()`) is preserved.

### DLL hot-reload sequence

```cpp
// 1. Serialize living entities (snapshot or raw binary)
// 2. Unload old DLL; load new DLL
// 3. Install shared context in the new module
SetTypeContext(sharedCtx);
// 4. Refresh descriptors for recompiled components
componentRegistry->ReRegisterComponent<MyComponent>();
// 5. Deserialize -- IDs are stable across the reload
```

`TypeID_v` (a static-init template variable that was a DLL footgun) is removed; use `Astra::TypeID<T>::Value()` instead (IDs resolve through the active TypeContext).

## Container Fixes & Fuzzing

New differential fuzz suites (21 fuzz tests covering FlatMap/FlatSet churn with adversarial hashing, SmallVector spill-boundary, and Bitmap bulk ops) found two correctness bugs in the internal containers.

### FlatMap / FlatSet duplicate-insertion bug

`Emplace` inserted a key at the **first empty-or-deleted (tombstone) slot** encountered during the probe chain before completing the duplicate scan. Because tombstones do not terminate the probe sequence, a key already present later in the chain could be inserted a second time, causing a silent size overcount and returning iterators to two distinct slots for the same logical key.

**Fix:** defer slot selection until an **EMPTY** slot terminates the scan. If a matching key is found during the scan, return the existing slot (no insert). Only after confirming no duplicate exists is the deferred slot used for insertion.

### SwissTable H2 metadata-range hazard

`SwissTable::H2` extracted the top 7 bits of the hash via `& 0x7F`, which already excluded the `0x80` sentinel. However, a degenerate hasher whose top 7 bits are all zero produces H2 == 0, which falls outside the range `[1, 127]` that `Group::Match` assumes for probe bytes, breaking the SIMD match logic.

**Fix:** H2 now folds `0` to `1` centrally (`return h2 == 0 ? 1 : h2`) so any hasher is guaranteed to produce a value in `[1, 127]`.

## Cross-Compiler & CI

Approximately 25 portability fixes were required to build cleanly under current gcc and clang (verified locally with gcc 15.1 / clang 18):

- Dependent-name disambiguators (`typename` / `template`) in templated base-class member access.
- Removed in-class partial specialisations (not permitted by the standard; MSVC accepted them as an extension).
- Fixed member-initialiser order to match declaration order (gcc `-Wreorder`).
- Corrected attribute placement (`[[nodiscard]]` before `inline`, not after).
- Warning hygiene: signed/unsigned comparisons, unused parameters, shadow declarations.

A GitHub Actions CI matrix (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs on every push to every branch and on every pull request:

| Job | Compiler | Standard |
|-----|----------|----------|
| windows-msvc | MSVC on windows-latest | C++20 |
| linux-gcc | current distro gcc on ubuntu-latest (unpinned) | C++20 |
| linux-clang | current distro clang on ubuntu-latest (unpinned) | C++20 |

Compilers are unpinned (distro-default on ubuntu-latest and MSVC on windows-latest). Verified locally with gcc 15.1 / clang 18. All three jobs build in Release, run the full 496-test suite, and must be green before merge.

- Fixed `CreateEntityWith` examples to match the actual API signature.
- Added **Threading Model** section documenting the scheduler seam and default-sequential behaviour.

---

## Removals

| Removed | Replacement | Reason |
|---------|-------------|--------|
| `TypeID_v<T>` (static template variable) | `Astra::TypeID<T>::Value()` | Static-init order fiasco across DLL boundaries |
| `MakeComponentMask` constexpr overload | Runtime `ComponentMask` construction | `Bitmap` is not a literal type under clang; constexpr was misleading |

---

## Requirements

- C++20 compatible compiler (MSVC 2022+, GCC 11+, Clang 13+)
- Premake5 for project generation
- Optional: GoogleTest, Google Benchmark
